messages:
incident-bot: Incident created: observability.ingest.delay detected for datadog.us-west-2. Severity: P2. Pager auto-notified SRE rota. https://status.datadoghq.com/updates (link)
sam_sre: seeing high tail latency on dd-forwarder metrics, dashboards show >10min lag. traces are mostly arriving but a lot of histogram gaps. beginning triage.
ben_oncall: confirmed. Alerts firing for: metrics_missing_rate and logs_ingest_backpressure. Customers reporting missing live-monitoring data. Paging now to eng-sre.
alice_ops: working hypothesis: Datadog ingestion pipeline in us-west-2 is throttling — forwarding buffer in our logging agent is filling. Rolling up immediate mitigations.
julie_cs: received first CS ticket: "We lost alerting for our production cluster, pages show blank graphs." Customer impacted: 3 enterprise customers in us-west. Escalating support tickets and notifying AMs.
datadog-bot: Datadog status page update: "Ingestion delays affecting metrics and logs in US-WEST region. Engineers investigating. ETA unknown." (link)
sam_sre: quick mitigations: 1) increase local agent disk buffer to avoid tail drop, 2) flip logs->s3 fallback for critical audit logs, 3) enable sampling for debug-level logs. Applying now.
alice_ops: pushing config change to logging agents (canary to 2 hosts) — command:
```
kubectl -n infra set env ds/log-agent DD_BUFFER_MAX_SIZE=2048MB --overwrite
kubectl -n infra apply -f log-to-s3-fallback.yaml
```
will monitor for backpressure metrics.
ben_oncall: opened support case with Datadog (case #DD-2024-0427), requested priority escalation and pointer to incident. Sent them example missing metric ids.
julie_cs: notifying the three impacted customers with an incident note: short summary + mitigation + ETA unknown. Keeping ticket owners updated.
morgan_pm: flagging on product side — any feature flags we should flip to reduce telemetry? Also need customer comms template. Will draft.
sam_sre: observed partial recovery: metrics lag down to ~3-5min on canary hosts, but overall ingestion still sporadic. Keep fallback active for critical streams.
alice_ops: scheduling a controlled throttle of non-critical logs from internal infra to free capacity:
```
# throttle rule
label: nonprod-debug
action: drop 80% if datadog.region==us-west-2 and priority==debug
```
applying now.
ben_oncall: Datadog responded: "Investigating a broker-side queueing issue; customers may see delayed processing. No customer data loss expected. Will update." They're asking for our sampling/agent config to reproduce.
sam_sre: uploaded agent configs to the support ticket and asked for expected ingestion lag windows. Also requested a post-incident RCA once resolved.
julie_cs: updated customer notices with "next update in 30 min" and included mitigation steps we took. Several customers replied with logs they'd like saved — coordinating with ops to preserve.
morgan_pm: action item: postmortem owner? Recommend eng-sre + ops co-author. Also want runbook updates: add fallback-to-s3 step and explicit vendor-contact template.
ben_oncall: handing off to night oncall (sam_sre -> night: @ben_oncall_night) — current state: mitigations applied, partial recovery, Datadog investigating, customer comms sent. Please monitor until cleared or vendor resolves.
sam_sre: ack handoff. I'll post a summary and follow up in 1h if no vendor progress. leaving a brief checklist in thread:
- [x] open vendor case
- [x] enable s3 fallback for critical logs
- [x] increase agent buffers (canary applied)
- [ ] confirm full ingestion recovery
- [ ] vendor RCA requested
- [ ] update runbook with new steps

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated_partial, severity=P2, assignees=[ben_oncall, sam_sre].
ben_oncall: (reaction :thumbsup:) will monitor overnight and escalate to datadog oncall if we see queue growth again.
